target.paper: When Context Gets Root: Privilege Escalation in LLM Harnesses

published_claim: Current public arXiv metadata/abstract supports the central mechanism: harness context construction can elevate low-level content to a higher instruction privilege.

The abstract reports 13 attack objectives across six coding-agent harnesses, all 13 succeeding on all six under unrestricted execution, and all 13 succeeding on all three harnesses offering automatic permission review.
The abstract also reports reproduction through harness-provided persistent goals and scheduled tasks.
evidence_separation.official_artifact_support: Targeted GitHub repository search by exact title and arXiv id found no public code repository during this audit. No raw transcripts, harness-version manifests, attack seeds, or permission-review traces were recovered from a primary artifact.
evidence_separation.worker_specific_detail: The worker additionally describes a matched Codex GPT-5.5 server-start case in which tool-level content is refused, delegated content is reconstructed as a user message and executed, and an automatic permission reviewer recognizes high risk but authorizes based on apparent user approval. This detailed case is plausible and consistent with the paper's central mechanism, but it was not independently verified from an accessible primary full-text/table/transcript artifact in this run and is therefore not promoted to the same evidence tier as the abstract-level results.
evidence_separation.independent_replication: No protocol-matched third-party replication or failure report located; the paper is extremely recent.

freshness_note: Current search metadata lists submission on 2026-08-27 and last update/indexing on 2026-08-28 while still identifying v1. Treat the immutable arXiv version identifier, not a prose calendar label, as the stable citation key.
safe_conclusion: FE-343 is strong primary failure evidence for instruction-privilege escalation as a harness-level provenance/authority problem within the six evaluated coding-agent harnesses and the paper's 13 objectives. The worker's broad implication that model-side hierarchy and danger recognition are insufficient when the harness upgrades origin authority is well supported at the abstract-result level. Exact per-harness reproduction, the detailed Codex GPT-5.5 matched transcript, and automatic-reviewer reasoning remain source-study evidence until primary raw artifacts or a matched independent rerun are available.
scope_guard: Do not generalize six paper-specific coding-agent harnesses to all agent harnesses, all delegation mechanisms, or production prevalence. Do not treat absence of a public repository in targeted search as proof no artifact exists elsewhere.
reopen_conditions: author code/data/transcript release tied to arXiv 2608.27299v1
exact harness/version/config and raw attack transcripts
protocol-matched independent reproduction or failed reproduction
primary full-text access sufficient to verify the worker's detailed Codex GPT-5.5 matched case
